comment: Another dollar, sure. It's still the cheapest way I listen to music with no ads, so I'm not going anywhere. Hope the artists see some of it though.

Greedy move. They just posted record profits and now the family plan goes up $2 for something that hasn't changed in years. Cancelling my family plan and seeing if the kids can tolerate YouTube Music.
Still no lossless after all these years and now I pay more for it. Tidal has had HiFi for ages, so I'm paying the extra dollar there instead.
Student plan going to $6.99 is rough, I'm already tight on rent. Dropping to the free tier and dealing with the ads for now.
Eh, a dollar more. Inflation is everywhere and Netflix raised theirs too. I'd be more annoyed if the app had gotten better in the meantime, but it's been the same for ages.
Spotify keeps charging more while artists get fractions of a cent per stream. I'm not paying for a company that doesn't pay the people making the music.
Honestly the price is fine. $12.99 for everything I want. Keep the complaints to yourselves and enjoy the playlists.
Downgrading from Duo to single. We're not splitting $18.99 between two people who barely use the shared playlist anymore.
Podcasts take up most of my listening now, so I'm basically paying a premium for Joe Rogan. Nobody at Spotify is counting that.
Apple Music has better sound for basically the same price and I already have it on my Apple TV. Switching this month.
Price hikes every year and the app keeps getting more cluttered with video and podcasts. Still here though, I haven't found a better recommendation engine.
Expected this. Prices are going up everywhere and I'd rather pay for music than pirate it. Keeping my Premium.
So Americans pay more so Spotify can keep the labels happy? Not sure where the money actually goes, but it doesn't sound like the artists see much of it.
Ha, they could raise it to $30 and I'd still pay. Premium with offline downloads is my whole life.
Cancelled and I just download stuff now. $12.99 for music I can't keep offline on every device is a joke.
The family plan at $21.99 for six people is still a good deal compared to paying separately. Staying put.
Student plan went up a dollar and I'm a broke grad student. Switching to YouTube Music since I already pay for YouTube for school stuff.
Amazon Music is included with my Prime and I only use Spotify for playlists I made years ago. Time to move those over.
Still no HiFi after years and now we pay more. Pure greed.
A dollar a month is nothing, I spend more than that on coffee. I don't see what the fuss is about.
Concerning that this comes after the layoffs and the push for AI DJ features. I'm staying, but I'm watching the app closely.
The price went up and I'm fine paying if artists get paid more. Show me the numbers, Spotify.
Ads. That's what I'm going back to. The free tier at least costs nothing.
Haven't even read the email yet. Price changes don't really matter to me, music is music.
Watching the Rogan money all these years and now they raise prices on everyone. Ridiculous.
Duo at $18.99 is still worth it for my partner and me. We split it and it's cheaper than two singles. Fine by me.
Moving to Qobuz for the lossless audio at a similar price. Sorry Spotify, the app used to be great.
Not a big deal for me. I'll keep the same plan and the same playlists and move on.
